Lead vehicle-offer link creation and multi-channel dispatch
Collision-retried 8-char offer short code (unambiguous alphabet)
Rationale: BOOKING_BASE_URL_TEMPLATE lets the same function point at prod, preview, ngrok or a test domain without a code change
Rationale: dispatch outcome is captured and returned so the caller shows a truthful toast instead of always claiming 'Offer sent'
Lead stage transition to vehicle_offered (DB trigger emits lead.stage_changed)
Booking pre-authorisation checkout (manual capture hold, not a charge)
Rationale: some Connect accounts are not eligible for extended_authorization even on 'if_available', so card feature variants are downgraded rather than failing booking
Rationale: preauth_expires_at is a conservative FLOOR, never the truth — the real capture deadline only exists after authorisation and is reconciled by the Stripe webhook
Bonzah insurance premium as a second checkout line item
Pending payments row written at session creation, settled later by the Stripe webhook
One-shot sales/super-admin tenant provisioning (tenant, login, palette, paywall, CMS)
Rationale: every fallible check runs BEFORE the tenant insert so a typo costs a 400, never a provision-then-rollback
Staged rollback with orphan bookkeeping (delete tenant/auth user/app_user, suspend on failure)
Deterministic first-login password derived from the slug's alphanumerics
Slug / company-name / email uniqueness guards, with unique_violation closing the check-then-insert race
Free-text and structured opening hours mapped onto the tenants day/working-hours columns
Location text to IANA timezone, with the comma-anchored state slot beating a bare abbreviation ('LA, CA' must not be Louisiana)
Booking-site CMS section seeding and publication for the new tenant
Rationale: unpublished pages fall through to Drive247's own copy, phone and privacy text on the client's site — so the generated copy states only what the form actually said
Rationale: stripe_mode and bonzah_mode stay on 'test' for both tenant types, and subscription_account must be 'uae' (hardcoding 'uk' silently billed new tenants on the legacy account)
Live 0-day subscription plan created as the hard paywall (any failure rolls the tenant back)
Rationale: without explicit identity columns the tenant renders the platform default app_name 'Drive 917' verbatim in sidebar, login and title
Rationale: contentSeeded is only true when every generated page landed — 'sections > 0' was a lie when only the site-settings shell existed
Platform subscription checkout (Drive247 billing its tenants)
Rationale: Stripe consent_collection is the only non-bypassable ToS gate but 400s unless a ToS URL is set on all four account/mode combos, so it is env-gated OFF
Rationale: acceptedTos is deliberately not a hard requirement — a client boolean has no evidentiary value, and rejecting would lock tenants out of an inescapable paywall during a deploy skew
Rationale: only the operator can accept the operator's contract — a super admin driving checkout must not mint a consent record
Write-once platform-ToS stamp enforced by .is('platform_tos_accepted_at', null) on the UPDATE rather than a read-then-write
Rationale: never SELECT platform_tos_accepted_at — PostgREST fails the whole query on an unknown column and the guard turns that into 'Tenant not found' for every checkout
Rationale: reuse an existing Stripe customer (retries spawned three customers for one tenant in a morning) but drop a foreign one after a uk-uae migration; also what makes test clocks usable
upfront_monthly billing model — first charge anchored to subscription_billing_anchor one calendar month after go-live, ridden on Stripe's trial primitive without calling it a trial
$1 card-verification line item added ONLY when the first real charge is deferred, else the webhook's refund would return the whole first invoice
Rationale: the metered e-sign price is attached silently by the webhook, not as a checkout line item that renders a confusing duplicate product row
Plan price re-created when it does not exist on the tenant's current subscription account/mode
Rationale: a 0-day plan must send NEITHER trial key — Stripe rejects trial_period_days:0 with a 400 that surfaced as a generic non-2xx and blocked checkout entirely
Stripe billing-portal session for updating the tenant's payment method

Rationale: the live subscription row is authoritative for the Stripe customer, tenants.stripe_subscription_customer_id is only a hint — a stale but VALID id opened a portal for a customer with no subscription and the tenant's re-saved card never took
Self-healing repair of tenants.stripe_subscription_customer_id so later lookups agree
Portal configuration deliberately allows payment-method update and invoice history only — cancellation goes through support
UK to UAE subscription migration capture (super admin generates, operator pays)
Rationale: UAE trial_end is set to the UK subscription's current_period_end so the already-paid period is honoured — zero double billing, with a 48-hour Stripe minimum fallback to immediate billing
Plan auto-resolution and mirroring so legacy subscriptions with no plan_id can still self-serve migration at their existing price
Dual authorization: super admin for any tenant, head_admin/admin only for their own — a non-super-admin's caller-supplied tenantId is overwritten, never trusted
Rationale: the migration link is generated by a super admin but the OPERATOR enters the card, so consent can only come from Stripe's own gate; tos_version rides metadata inertly until the gate is on
Nothing is stored prematurely — the webhook flips tenants.subscription_account to 'uae' and sets the UK subscription to cancel_at_period_end on checkout.session.completed
Installment-plan upfront (deposit and fees) checkout
Rationale: Stripe customers are scoped per account+mode, so a stored id is validated before reuse or sessions.create fails with 'No such customer'
setup_future_usage off_session saves the card so later installments can be charged unattended
Veriff identity-verification session creation
Two entry shapes: portal (existing customerId, row persisted) vs booking flow (customerDetails only, nothing stored until the customer exists)
Per-tenant verification_document_type mapped to Veriff DRIVERS_LICENSE / PASSPORT / ID_CARD
Tenant-branded Supabase Auth emails via the Send Email hook and Resend
Rationale: signup and recovery emails are skipped here because those flows are handled by the OTP functions
Tenant resolution chain: user_metadata, then customer_users, then app_users, then a Drive 247 default
Client redirect_to only honoured when it is a real production URL, otherwise rebuilt from the tenant slug
Trax customer-facing AI assistant (gpt-4o-mini, stateless, account data only)
Rationale: CORS, OpenAI and currency helpers are inlined because this function must deploy with no shared-module dependencies (MCP deployment)
Rationale: when the tenant hides plates the registration is stripped where the RPC and fallback paths converge, and withheld fail-closed when the tenant row could not be read at all
Rationale: hide_vehicle_registration is not in every deployment, so an unknown-column failure retries without it rather than costing the tenant name and currency in every chat
Per-call OpenAI token and USD cost logging
CHART_DATA fenced block protocol letting the model emit a renderable chart alongside prose
Customer account creation linking auth.users to customer_users to customers
Rationale: an auth user with no customer link for this tenant is reclaimed (password reset, email confirmed) instead of dead-ending the signup-says-exists / login-says-no-customer loop
Cleanup deletes only a freshly-created auth user, never a reclaimed orphan
Daily payment-reminder generation from unpaid ledger charges
Reminder schedule: 2 days ahead, due today, 1 day overdue, then weekly to 4 weeks
Reminder suppressed when the customer's open Credit entries already cover the charge
Rationale: only_rental_id scopes a Time-Machine sandbox dispatch to one rental so a manual run can never touch another tenant's charges; absent means the unchanged global cron
Same-day idempotence — one reminder per charge and type per calendar day
Operator dashboard KPI aggregation (overdue, due today, active rentals, fines, revenue, utilisation)
60-second in-memory per-isolate cache keyed on the date range
Promise.allSettled so one failing KPI query degrades that tile instead of the whole dashboard
Gotcha: the KPI queries carry no tenant filter and the cache key omits the tenant, so figures are computed service-role-wide across all tenants
Deduct an excess-mileage charge from the security deposit

Rationale: a Stripe partial capture AUTO-RELEASES the uncaptured remainder and it cannot be captured later — deducting $200 of a $1,500 hold silently released $1,300 while the row still claimed full cover
Remainder preserved via multicapture on the same PaymentIntent, else re-authorised on the saved card as a rollover hold

Rationale: verify_jwt is not authorization — the gateway accepts the public anon key as a valid JWT and booking customers authenticate against the same project, so anyone could pull money off another renter's card
Rationale: the hold's own recorded mode and Connect account win over the tenant row, which may have flipped mid-rental and would send the capture to an account that never heard of the PaymentIntent
deposit_hold_links upsert as the authorization ledger — full replacement, best-effort, keyed on (rental_id, attempt_seq, action) so it means 'the latest capture against this link'
Fail-closed reconciliation: a PaymentIntent no longer in requires_capture flips the rental to 'expired' and refuses rather than falling through to claw back an unrelated captured payment
Rationale: the rental row is the authority on its own tenant — a body tenantId is ignored so a caller cannot mis-file ledger and hold-link rows under a tenant they chose
Legacy fallback: when the deposit was charged rather than held, a partial Stripe refund plus a Refund ledger entry
Delete a tenant's Stripe Connect account (disconnect)
Gotcha: this destructive endpoint has no caller authorization and uses a single global STRIPE_SECRET_KEY instead of the shared dual-mode/dual-platform Stripe helpers
Licence-plate region detection for photo redaction (AWS Rekognition DetectText)

Rationale: measured on eight real photos DetectText found ZERO plates, so 'nothing found' is the normal answer and a false positive (painting over the wrong part of a customer's photo) is worse than returning nothing
Glyph canonicalisation (O/0, I/1, S/5, B/8, Z/2) for MATCHING ONLY — the operator is always shown the raw detection
Adjacent-word merge that rebuilds a plate OCR split across two WORD detections, covering the union of their boxes
Union of the axis-aligned box and rotated polygon, padded more when the quad fill ratio says the plate is skewed
Rationale: original_url is preferred because re-detecting on an already-masked photo_url finds nothing
Role gate (head_admin/admin/manager or super admin) plus explicit tenant scoping so the button and the API agree on who may act and 403 differs from 404
AI handover-vs-return photo comparison producing a new-damage report
Magic-byte format detection with AVIF/HEIC transcoded to JPEG through the wsrv.nl proxy because OpenAI Vision rejects them
Deliberately strict prompt and output clamping — dirt, lighting and angle differences must not be reported, and confidence is lowered rather than speculating
Regeneration upserts on rental_id and resets the reviewer fields so a stale human sign-off never survives a new report
Emergency bootstrap: resets one hardcoded admin auth user to a hardcoded temporary password
Gotcha: no caller authorization, a hardcoded project URL, a hardcoded admin user id and a fixed temp password returned in the response body — a live account-takeover surface if deployed
Super-admin password reset tool (forces must_change_password)

Rationale: this endpoint previously had NO authorization and the portal's 'Forgot password?' called it directly — anyone knowing a staff email could take over the account; recovery now belongs to the email-verified flow
Rationale: listUsers is paginated (default 50) and the store lowercases addresses, so the old unpaginated case-sensitive lookup reported 'User not found' for anyone past user 50 or with mixed case
Brand-colour preview endpoint turning free text into a tenant palette
Caller must be an active super admin or sales agent (is_sales_agent), the same gate the sales onboarding function uses
Cross-cutting hazard: the Supabase gateway accepts the public anon key as a valid JWT, so verify_jwt alone authorizes nothing on money and account endpoints
Cross-cutting pattern: Stripe customer and price ids belong to ONE account+mode, so every id read out of the database is verified (and re-minted) before use
Cross-cutting hazard: PostgREST fails the WHOLE select on one unknown column, so functions deployed ahead of a migration must not name new columns
